body: Tuesday, February 10 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-10 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: Activity is firm: the January ISM manufacturing PMI printed 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02]. Labour is cracking: December job openings fell to the lowest since 2020 while layoffs edged up Bloomberg.com [Feb 05]. The Fed's Daly calls the job market 'precarious' and eyes rate cuts Reuters [Feb 06]. Growth is fine, labour is the swing factor, and the Fed holds until payrolls force its hand.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.48% and the 10Y at 4.22%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 74 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 6 bps and the 10Y rose 4 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-09). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and the 20-observation move is a steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat), matching bets on a steeper curve under a Warsh-led Fed Reuters [Feb 04]. The S&P 500 closed at 6,964.82, flat over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 17.36 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

New / Most Important: The shutdown-delayed January payrolls report lands on Feb. 11, with inflation and retail sales data also due CNBC [Feb 04] Investopedia [Feb 08]. It follows a 'breathtaking' $660bn Big Tech AI spending guide and a $1 trillion one-week software rout Financial Times [Feb 06] Reuters [Feb 05]. Goldman says hedge funds added record shorts on US stocks, yet the Russell 2000 is up 2.47% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09) Bloomberg.com [Feb 09].

Playbook ✓: Stay long industrials, energy and staples over mega-cap software, and hold 2Y Treasuries into payrolls, since a weak print extends the steepener. Hedge with short-dated S&P 500 puts while the VIX is at 17.36 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Change the call if strong payrolls push the 2Y back above 3.54%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-09).

Macro Stance: The ECB held rates while the UK tilted toward a cut, so Europe's policy bias now points to easing rather than tightening Bloomberg.com [Feb 07]. With euro-zone inflation down to 1.7% in January, below the 2% target, the ECB has room to respond if the strong euro bites Financial Times [Feb 04]. That backdrop supports European equities and duration.

Activity & Inflation: German factory orders posted their biggest increase in two years, the first hard sign that industry is turning Reuters [Feb 05]. EUR/USD closed at 1.1826, up 1.74% over 20 sessions, a disinflationary headwind for exporters, and the STOXX 600 rose 1.71% to 621.41 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

New / Most Important: Europe and Asia led global equity fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure, the clearest evidence yet that the rotation is global Reuters [Feb 06]. The FTSE 100 closed at 10,386.20, up 2.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Playbook ✓: Overweight continental banks, insurers and domestic cyclicals, funded from US mega-cap tech; add Bund duration on back-ups, since the next ECB move is more likely a cut than a hike. Avoid exporters most exposed to the strong euro, autos first. Change the call if German orders reverse or the euro's rise forces a growth downgrade.

Macro Stance: China is running two economies: a strong currency and an export-tech complex on one side, a property and consumption slump on the other. Beijing is signalling a trimmed GDP growth target that requires less stimulus, which tells us policy will stay targeted rather than broad Bloomberg.com [Feb 05]. We stay Mixed: long the currency and AI-hardware leaders, underweight property and consumption until credit turns.

PMIs & Activity: The official January manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3, back in contraction, while the private survey showed factory expansion accelerating Reuters [Jan 30] Reuters [Feb 01]. The split says large, state-linked manufacturers are struggling while private exporters carry the cycle. Confirmation of weakness would be a second official reading below 50 with a fading private gauge; confirmation of recovery would be the official index back above 50.

Credit Impulse: The feed carries no January credit or aggregate financing print, so the impulse cannot be confirmed yet. The visible policy signal is about keeping liquidity at home: regulators urged banks to curb exposure to US Treasuries Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]. With the growth target trimmed and stimulus needs lower, we assume a flat-to-modest impulse; a jump in household medium-term loans would be the first sign of a real turn.

Property: Property is getting worse, not better: S&P says China's property slump will be worse than it expected this year CNBC [Feb 09]. Shanghai is piloting state home purchases in three districts to halt the slide, a stock-absorption tool rather than demand stimulus Caixin Global [Feb 05]. Stay underweight developers and property-heavy banks; a nationwide state-purchase programme funded from the centre would change that call.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal policy is rationed rather than expansive, consistent with a lower growth target Bloomberg.com [Feb 05]. Financial policy is tightening at the edges: Beijing barred unapproved yuan-linked stablecoins abroad Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. On trade, the US proposed a critical-minerals trade bloc aimed at countering China, which keeps rare earths and processing capacity at the centre of the rivalry and gives Beijing leverage over Western supply chains Reuters [Feb 04].

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 27,027.16, up 1.57% over 20 sessions, while the Shanghai Composite closed at 4,123.09, down 1.01% over 20 sessions despite a 1.41% gain in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). ASHR closed at 34.10, up 0.56% over 20 sessions, and KWEB at 34.34, down 4.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). USD/CNY closed at 6.9388, down 0.55% over 20 sessions, with the yuan at its strongest since 2023 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09) Bloomberg.com [Feb 09].

New / Most Important: The yuan's run is the story: it advanced to its strongest since 2023 after regulators told banks to curb US Treasury exposure, which reads as gradual diversification away from dollar assets Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]. Equity demand is selective but deep: chip designer Montage Technology soared 64% in its Hong Kong debut Reuters [Feb 09]. Capital is flowing to AI hardware and away from consumer internet.

Playbook ✓: Own CNY strength via short USD/CNY and AI-hardware names where IPO demand is deep Reuters [Feb 09]; avoid developers and Hong Kong internet, with KWEB down 4.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Add on a credit print showing household loan growth or a broader state home-purchase programme; cut if the official PMI stays in contraction and the yuan reverses. ⚠ Divergence: the private PMI shows factory expansion accelerating even as the official PMI fell to 49.3 Reuters [Feb 01] Reuters [Jan 30], so exporters, not Beijing's stimulus, are holding the cycle up.

Macro Stance: Sanae Takaichi's LDP won a two-thirds supermajority in the Lower House, a clear mandate for her fiscal agenda The Japan Times [Feb 09]. Markets gave her the benefit of the doubt: long bonds rallied as the win eased fiscal concerns Bloomberg.com [Feb 09]. A BOJ board member added to signals pointing to rate hikes, so policy is shifting to fiscal push plus gradual tightening The Japan Times [Feb 06].

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at a record 56,363.94, up 3.89% in the prior session and 8.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). USD/JPY closed at 157.24, down 0.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09), and the election added to the 'Sell America' pressure on the dollar MarketWatch [Feb 09].

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities with a tilt to banks and defence, which benefit from BOJ hikes and the security agenda; keep the yen hedge light because the dollar is under broad pressure. Change the call if super-long JGB yields resume rising, which would mean the market has withdrawn its benefit of the doubt on Takaichi's spending.

Macro Stance: The RBA delivered a rate hike and signalled more on the horizon WSJ [Feb 03]. It has also issued a dire warning on growth, so it is tightening into a slowdown to stamp out inflation AFR [Feb 09]. A hawkish central bank with a weakening household sector favours resources over domestic cyclicals.

Demand & Financing: Household spending fell in December after two strong months, so demand was already cooling before the hike Reuters [Feb 08]. AUD/USD closed at 0.7034, up 5.2% over 20 sessions, tightening financial conditions further (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). The ASX 200 closed at 8,912.10, up 2.33% in the prior session and 2.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Playbook ✓: Own resources and gold miners, whose commodity tailwinds outweigh the stronger AUD's translation hit; underweight rate-sensitive retailers and builders into reporting season. Change the call if the RBA signals a pause after its growth warning, which would revive housing-linked stocks.

Monetary & Activity: The RPP left rates unchanged in February, extending its pause Bankier.pl [Feb 04]. The NBP projection puts inflation in line with target, and key decisions are flagged for March Business Insider Polska [Feb 06]. Growth is solid after GDP rose 3.6% in 2025 xyz.pl [Jan 31]. On-target inflation, solid growth and still-high real rates keep a March cut alive, which supports domestic equities and the bond market.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5645, down 1.59% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2153, up 0.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). EPOL closed at 38.76, up 7.07% over 20 sessions and 2.22% in the prior session, and the WIG20TR tracker at 68.24, up 4.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Pekao is up 9.43%, PKO BP 5.72% and PZU 2.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Companies: An Advent- and FedEx-led consortium agreed to buy parcel-locker firm InPost for $9.2 billion, a valuation marker for Polish consumer platforms Reuters [Feb 09]. Orlen is up 11.34% and KGHM 6.01% over 20 sessions, while Allegro is down 10.11% and Dino 6.6%; CD Projekt rose 3.67% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Security & New Development: Russia accused Poland of involvement in an assassination attempt on a general in Moscow, a reminder that the eastern-flank risk premium is not going away Notes From Poland [Feb 09]. The new development for markets is legal: the EU Court of Justice rules on WIBOR on 12 February, which Bankier frames as a possible breakthrough for borrowers and a binary risk for banks Bankier.pl [Feb 09].

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Polish equities via EPOL, tilting to insurers (PZU) and energy over banks into the WIBOR ruling; add banks on a benign verdict. ⚠ Divergence: Pekao is up 9.43% and PKO BP 5.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09) even as a CJEU ruling that could hit WIBOR-linked mortgage books is days away Bankier.pl [Feb 09].

Narrative: Consensus has flipped from 'AI lifts all tech' to 'AI eats software': US software stocks lost $1 trillion in a week on AI-disruption fears Reuters [Feb 05]. Microsoft is down 13.7% and Oracle 21.12% over 20 sessions, and XLK closed at 143.35, down 1.92% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Palantir beat estimates and the stock rallied, proof that AI winners with visible revenue still get paid CNBC [Feb 03]. Even so, PLTR is down 19.48% over 20 sessions despite a 5.16% jump in the prior session, which shows how far the sector-wide de-rating has run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

EPS Upside Watch: Hardware owners of the capex flow carry the estimate upside: with Big Tech guiding to $660bn of AI spending, Nvidia (190.04, up 2.8% over 20 sessions) and Broadcom (343.94) sell the picks and shovels (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09) Financial Times [Feb 06].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Goldman says hedge funds added record shorts in the rout, and in the prior session Oracle jumped 9.64% and Microsoft 3.11% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09) Bloomberg.com [Feb 09]. Crowded shorts in beaten-down software set up a squeeze; do not press the downside, and use rallies to rotate into hardware.

Narrative: Capex intensity is the debate: Alphabet's dollar bond sale drew over $100 billion of demand to fund record spending Bloomberg.com [Feb 09]. XLC closed at 116.88, down 0.87% over 20 sessions, with GOOGL down 5.64% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Alphabet beat on revenue but projects a significant AI spending increase, and Roblox jumped 16% after its report CNBC [Feb 04] Barron's [Feb 06]. Engagement platforms with clean beats were paid; capex-heavy platforms were not.

EPS Upside Watch: Meta is up 3.7% over 20 sessions and 2.38% in the prior session, the strongest of the megacap platforms in the group (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Ad-led platforms with AI-driven targeting carry estimate upside while ad budgets hold, and Meta is the cleanest expression.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Legacy media is losing even as platforms spend: Netflix is down 8.93% and Disney 7.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Investors are paying for distribution and AI-driven ad tools, not content libraries.

Narrative: Financials are AI collateral damage: private-credit stocks keep falling as the software wipeout spreads into lenders' books Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. XLF closed at 53.94, down 3.21% over 20 sessions, while JPM fell 2.15% and GS rose 0.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: UBS beat expectations with a $1.2 billion fourth-quarter profit and plans a $3 billion buyback CNBC [Feb 04]. European banks are returning capital aggressively while US alternative managers de-rate.

EPS Upside Watch: Money-centre banks: investors are ramping up bets on a steeper curve under a Warsh-led Fed, which lifts net interest margins Reuters [Feb 04]. JPM and BAC rose 4.53% and 4.4% over five sessions, the first sign the market is pricing that (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits in private credit, not bank equity: if software borrowers lose pricing power, private-credit marks will follow the listed vehicles lower Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. Own banks, avoid alternative managers and BDCs until marks are tested.

Narrative: Energy leads the 2026 rotation: XLE closed at 53.64, up 14.93% over 20 sessions, with XOM up 21.35% and CVX up 12.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Brent closed at 69.04 and WTI at 64.36, up 9% and 8.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Shell posted its weakest quarterly profit in nearly five years but kept buybacks steady CNBC [Feb 05]. The message is that majors defend distributions even as earnings fall, which supports the yield case for the group.

EPS Upside Watch: US integrateds: Exxon's 9.26% gain over five sessions shows the market chasing a higher crude deck, and first-quarter revisions should turn up for upstream-heavy names (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hedge funds lifted bullish oil bets to a 10-month high on Iran risks, so the move is positioning-driven and fragile to diplomacy Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. Natural gas fell 8.3% in the prior session, a reminder that the energy trade is not uniform (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Narrative: Industrials are the cleanest beneficiary of the rotation and the AI power build-out, backed by a 52.6% ISM manufacturing reading PR Newswire [Feb 02]. XLI closed at 173.70, up 7.27% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar is up 20.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Rockwell Automation lifted guidance as profit jumped, confirming factory-automation demand WSJ [Feb 05]. Boeing closed at 244.71, up 5.02% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

EPS Upside Watch: Power equipment: GE Vernova's Q4 gas turbine orders surged 74%, a backlog that converts into earnings over several years Utility Dive [Jan 30]. Grid and turbine suppliers should keep beating as data-centre demand rises.

⚡ Breaking Convention: GE Aerospace is down 1.51% over 20 sessions while Caterpillar is up 20.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). The market is paying for AI-power and construction exposure, not aerospace quality, so crowding in machinery is now the risk.

Narrative: Discretionary is the capex casualty: AMZN is down 15.63% over 20 sessions and XLY closed at 117.55, down 5.51% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Tesla is down 6.22% and Nike 5.32% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Amazon fell on an earnings miss and $200 billion of 2026 capex guidance CNBC [Feb 05]. The market is no longer willing to fund retail-plus-cloud capex without visible returns, and Amazon is the sector's largest weight.

EPS Upside Watch: Home Depot closed at 381.00, up 1.7% over 20 sessions, the steadiest large name in the sector (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Estimate upside is limited to housing-repair and value niches, and a labour-market crack would hit those too.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are beating discretionary by a wide margin, XLP up 10.32% versus XLY down 5.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). That is a late-cycle signal that clashes with a firm ISM; either the labour data or the factory data is wrong, and payrolls decide.

Narrative: Staples are the rotation's winner: XLP closed at 87.43, up 10.32% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 12.65% and Costco 7.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Investors are paying for earnings visibility in a market punishing capex.
Reported: PepsiCo beat on earnings and revenues with strength across segments Yahoo Finance [Feb 04]. Pricing plus volume is the formula the market is rewarding.
EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola reports Tuesday and traders are pricing a post-earnings move Investopedia [Feb 07]. KO's pricing power makes it the cleanest beat candidate in the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Barron's says consumer staples look pricey and points to high yielders such as Clorox instead Barron's [Feb 09]. After a 10.32% run in 20 sessions, valuation is now the risk (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Narrative: Healthcare is two-speed: GLP-1 leaders compound while insurers de-rate. XLV closed at 156.32, down 0.63% over 20 sessions, with UNH down 19.85% and LLY down 1.78% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Reported: Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound pushed Q4 revenue up 46%, while Novo Nordisk sank 17% after a bleak 2026 forecast BioSpace [Feb 04] Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 04]. Share in obesity drugs is shifting decisively to Lilly.

EPS Upside Watch: Lilly closed at 1,044.67, slightly down over 20 sessions despite the growth (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09), which leaves room for upward revisions if pricing holds. It is the sector's clearest earnings-momentum name.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The contrarian trade is managed care, not GLP-1s: UNH at 275.70 is down 19.85% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09), and any stabilisation in medical costs would re-rate it faster than Lilly can grow. Wait for a guidance reset before buying.

Narrative: Materials ride gold and the capex-metals bid: XLB closed at 52.18, up 8.12% over 20 sessions, with Newmont up 10.77% and Freeport 12.52% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Gold closed at 5,079.40, up 12.85% over 20 sessions, and copper at 5.95 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).
Reported: The key materials news was corporate rather than earnings: Rio Tinto abandoned its Glencore merger Reuters [Feb 05]. Failed consolidation keeps copper supply growth scarce.

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners: with gold up 12.85% over 20 sessions, first-quarter margins for producers such as Newmont expand faster than costs (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Silver closed at 82.07, up 6.95% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Policy is becoming a demand source: the US proposed a critical-minerals trade bloc aimed at countering China Reuters [Feb 04]. Copper, the AI data-centre and grid metal, gains a strategic bid that does not depend on Chinese construction.

Narrative: REITs are a quiet rotation winner: XLRE closed at 42.25, up 4.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). US REITs ended January at a median 16.2% discount to NAV, which leaves room for take-privates and buybacks S&P Global [Feb 05].

Reported: The feed window carries no major US REIT result that moved the group; the sector traded on rates and rotation rather than earnings. The 10Y at 4.22%, up 4 bps over 20 observations, caps multiple expansion (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-09).

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and power-linked REITs ride the same AI capex wave as semis, while office and retail landlords lack an earnings catalyst. Discount-to-NAV names with buyback capacity carry the best FFO upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A rising 10Y is usually a REIT headwind, yet XLRE is up 4.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-09). Defensive rotation is overpowering rates, which makes the group vulnerable if payrolls surprise strong.

Narrative: Utilities split between regulated growers and merchant power: NextEra is up 12% over 20 sessions while Constellation is down 20.54% and Vistra 8.05% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). XLU closed at 43.48, up 2.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).
Reported: CMS Energy exceeded its 2025 guidance and raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance PR Newswire [Feb 05]. Regulated utilities are converting load growth into rate base and earnings.
EPS Upside Watch: Turbine and grid build-outs feed utility capex: GE Vernova's Q4 gas turbine orders surged 74%, a lead indicator for regulated rate-base growth Utility Dive [Jan 30].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The political backlash is building: New York Democrats proposed a sweeping pause on data-centre construction Politico [Feb 06]. That explains the merchant-power sell-off; own regulated names and avoid power merchants until data-centre siting rules settle.

Narrative: European autos are de-rating on the EV reset: Stellantis shares slumped over 20% after a $26.5 billion EV-related writedown Reuters [Feb 06]. The SXAP tracker closed at 44.63, down 5.27% over 20 sessions, and STLA is down 33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).
Reported: Volvo Cars fell over 22% in its worst trading day ever CNBC [Feb 05]. Two large producers resetting within days tells us EV transition costs are not yet fully in the price.

EPS Upside Watch: Relative winners are the German premium names: BMW is down 2.48%, Mercedes 2.46% and VOW3 1.56% over 20 sessions versus Renault's 7.15% fall (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Stronger balance sheets should let them absorb EV write-downs without cutting payouts.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Stellantis reset may be the template rather than the exception for mass-market producers Reuters [Feb 06]. A strong euro at 1.1826 adds a translation hit to exports (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

Narrative: Semis are the AI capex toll collector, with Big Tech guiding to $660bn of AI spending Financial Times [Feb 06]. SOXX closed at 352.77, up 7.3% over 20 sessions, with ASML up 12.22% and TSM up 9.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).
Reported: TSMC's January revenue jumped 37%, while AMD sank 17% after earnings Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] CNBC [Feb 04]. The market is paying for capacity and pricing power, not for share-gain promises.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and equipment: Micron is up 11.13% over 20 sessions despite a 12.4% drop over five, and ASML closed at 1,429.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Tight memory supply and lithography backlogs support upward revisions.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AMD at 216.00 is still up 6.31% over 20 sessions despite its post-earnings rout, and Intel is up 10.3% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). The market is buying the whole AI-compute complex rather than picking winners, which raises dispersion risk into Nvidia's next print.

Rewarded: Clean beats with visible monetisation: Palantir rallied after beating, and Roblox jumped 16% CNBC [Feb 03] Barron's [Feb 06]. PepsiCo beat across segments while staples led the tape Yahoo Finance [Feb 04].

Punished: Capex shocks and guidance misses: Amazon fell on a miss and $200 billion of capex guidance, AMD sank 17%, Novo sank 17% on a bleak forecast, and Stellantis slumped over 20% after its writedown CNBC [Feb 05] CNBC [Feb 04] Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 04] Reuters [Feb 06].

Pattern: The market pays for visibility, not the beat. AI-exposed incumbents were sold even on solid numbers as software lost $1 trillion in a week, and capex-heavy prints were sold unless paired with cash-flow comfort Reuters [Feb 05]. Staples and industrials with pricing power were the beneficiaries.

Attention into EPS: Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Cisco and Ford report alongside the delayed jobs, inflation and retail sales data Investopedia [Feb 08]. Robinhood, Rivian, AppLovin and Coinbase also have earnings, a read on retail trading and crypto activity Benzinga [Feb 09].

Playbook: Buy quality defensives and industrials into prints where guidance is the swing factor; fade capex-heavy names into results unless free-cash-flow guidance is explicit. Short AI-disruption losers only on relief bounces, given record shorts. The pattern breaks if a hyperscaler pairs higher capex with accelerating cloud revenue and the stock rallies.

Attention Gap: While oil gets the Iran headlines, Henry Hub fell 8.3% in the prior session to 3.14 and is roughly flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Yet the AI power build-out runs on gas turbines: GE Vernova's Q4 gas turbine orders surged 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30].

Exposure & Risk: Express it through gas-weighted producers and turbine and midstream suppliers rather than front-month futures, which carry weather noise. Risk: a mild end to winter and new LNG supply can keep prices pinned even as structural demand rises.

Attention Gap: The Takaichi trade is being expressed through the Nikkei, but banks are the cleaner play on a BOJ that keeps signalling hikes The Japan Times [Feb 06]. Higher policy rates lift lending margins directly, a tighter link to BOJ policy than exporters or defence names offer.

Exposure & Risk: Own the megabanks or a Japanese financials ETF, sized against a light yen hedge. Risk: a renewed super-long JGB sell-off would hit bond portfolios; the post-election rally in long bonds is the condition to watch Bloomberg.com [Feb 09].

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 70,120.78, down 3.97% over five sessions and 20.6% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Ether closed at 2,103.57, down 28.34%, and Solana at 86.70, down 31.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). IBIT closed at 40.11, COIN at 167.25 and MSTR at 138.44, down 12.01% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09).

New / Most Important: Capitulation markers stacked up: BlackRock's IBIT hit a record $10 billion of volume, which CoinDesk reads as capitulation CoinDesk [Feb 06]. Strategy bought another 1,142 BTC for $90 million with its treasury still below cost, so the largest corporate holder is under water but still buying The Block [Feb 09]. Policy cuts both ways: China barred unapproved yuan-linked stablecoins abroad Bloomberg.com [Feb 06].

Playbook: Scale into BTC via IBIT in thirds while volume washes out, and avoid leveraged products. Stay underweight ETH and SOL, which fell 28.34% and 31.03% over 20 sessions versus bitcoin's 20.6%, until they outperform on a bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-09). Change the call if Strategy stops buying or IBIT volume spikes again on a fresh low.
